core_idea: In fast-changing environments, advantage comes less from the resources a firm holds and more from its ability to integrate, build and reconfigure them. Dynamic capabilities are these higher-order capacities: sensing opportunities, seizing them and transforming the organization.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do firms adapt to technological or market change?
Which routines or managerial capacities allow organizations to renew themselves?
Typical data: longitudinal case studies, firm surveys, interviews with managers.
common_mistakes: Calling any capability 'dynamic'. Dynamic capabilities change other capabilities.
Defining the capability by its outcome (the firm adapted, so it had dynamic capabilities).
Ignoring the difference between Teece's view (source of lasting advantage) and Eisenhardt & Martin's (best-practice routines).

development.adds: Dynamic capabilities as identifiable routines; in high-velocity markets they are simple and experiential.
